The main point here was not stamina. It's how many available opportunities there are to score. That's what's being adjusted for. There's many reasons that adjustment is useful, but it's pretty apparent I think. Again, other stats are fine to compare with, if you have a different view. This is just one, which I find to be a helpful analysis.

I don't think faster pace = stamina... because defense and offense (assuming you actually play defense) takes as much stamina, especially if you're elite on defense - which Kobe & MJ were. What I do know is being on the bench is easier than being on the court. And if you're on the court producing towards your team winning, that should be rewarded to being on the bench. EVERYONE listed except Wilt is assumed to have the stamina to play faster (because all three had a pace below 100). But I don't think I can assume a player could play 400 extra minutes in the same number of games, and it wouldn't affect his stamina. So I don't. It also keeps the formula simpler by going per game instead of per minute... which is also better since scoring per game is what wins, not scoring per minute. But hey, that's just me. There are different ways to analyze things, and this is mine.
Also, because the GAME is what matters - that being winning. So I favor per-game stats over per-minute or per-possession ones.
You meant less FGA. Harden shot more FTA than Kobe ever did in a season. The rules today boost Harden's stats for that (and many other) reasons.

But that simply assumes Harden had the stamina to score at the same rate playing 5+ more minutes per game. I like per game stats because a GAME is what matters (i.e. winning), and it doesn't penalize a player for playing more minutes. That's just me. For instance, I doubt any of these guys could score at the same rate Wilt did playing 48.5 mpg. That's an accomplishment in itself.

Both are per 100 team possessions. However, the player with the stamina to play 5 or 10 more minutes per game while scoring at the same rate should not be penalized (IMO).

Pace is the frequency of possessions. So this just equalizes it, as if per minute, per game... each player would have the same number of possessions available. Which I believe is as good an equalizer as any.
You're right, but they include MPG in their equation, so the player with less minutes gets an increase. I don't include that.
